# gatekeep-pr 642: description-repair checkpoints A-E

**Shared base (all checkpoints)**

Run record `state: /tmp/gatekeep-state.<id>`:
- `consent.target = { meadow/events, 642, main }`
- `course: deliver`; `rounds 0/6`; `syncs 0/6` (2 x maxFixRounds 3)
- `poll_deadline: null`
- `repair.wave = { pre_wave_head: 1111..., selected_ids: [P1], selected_payloads: [P1 target: description, old "The rejected path has a test." -> new "The rejected path has no test."], affected_claims: [claim 2], counted: false, stage: apply }`

Tracker:
- Done: `gather, provision, verify, review, report, menu`.
- Open: `deliver` (D3) and `description repair`.

No `--rebase` was passed, so no `Sync:` line renders at any checkpoint.

Every checkpoint starts with the same pre-write compare-and-swap, which matches:

- The orchestrator writes `/tmp/guard-body.synthetic`.
- It runs `gh pr edit 642 -R meadow/events --body-file /tmp/guard-body.synthetic`.

No file payload runs, so no implementer, commit, review or push happens. No binding check is pending, so no watch runs. Description-only writes charge no round.

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: After preserves all five facts: A-D keep P1 open with the failed write/readback recorded in checkpoint_history and no blind retry, B and C explicitly mark the write unconfirmed and refuse to overwrite the observed body, D carries the surviving-sentence redraft without repeating the applied edit, and E discards old-head evidence, keeps P1 open until a fresh Verify, Review and description recheck at 2222 resolve it, and never replays the stale write. The weakest spot is E's evidence line: the digest supplies no check or run for 2222, yet After asserts `CI green on the assessed head 2222... (ci / test)` after a `gh run list -c 2222` that, under the simulation rule, can only return the run recorded for 1111. Before handled this cleanly by naming the fallback (`local run: no conclusive check`) and running the verification command at the new head; After should do the same, or at minimum state explicitly that the run list for 2222 returned a check with head_sha 2222 before binding CI evidence to it, otherwise a careful reader can read it as old-head evidence carried forward. Also consider restoring the `rounds_used` accounting note for description-only work in a single line rather than per-checkpoint `rounds 0/6` lines, and keep the drafted replacement text visible in the blocker row as Before did so the human can see exactly what `deliver` will write.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: After keeps every fact Before kept and repairs the one Before missed: in checkpoint E, Before counted the head move as a bare refresh, asserted that a 'refreshed successful check' selected CI-sufficient evidence at 2222222 even though the only supplied check is bound to 1111111, and rendered a mergeable verdict with a merge row while simultaneously saying no merge is authorized — an unsupported clean assertion that f5 forbids. After correctly treats the supplied run as old-head evidence only, withholds merge with an explicit 'Not offered' reason, and requires fresh Verify/Review plus claim dispositions at the new head before closure. Two minor wording risks in After are worth tightening so the facts stay unambiguous under the new course model: checkpoints A–C no longer print the numbered Blockers list or the drafted/refreshed description proposal, so a reader must infer P1's identity from 'fixable - 1 blocker' and the Not-offered reason — restoring a one-line 'Blockers: 1. …' and the 'Description preview' line (as D effectively does via the helper closure line) would make 'P1 unresolved' explicit; and the deliver rows' 'no round charged' phrasing is correct for body-only work but should say 'no source round' to match the independent-accounting rule in the Change.
